hypotheses.required_change: Increase mesh resolution through the thickness (more than 2 layers) and/or verify the extruded 3D solid model can actually represent out-of-plane bending/torsion physics at the load point and re-entrant corner with enough fidelity so the true stress state (and any singularity) is captured rather than being an artifact of a too-coarse through-thickness discretisation.

add_out_of_plane_hand_load_case.parameter_source: Engineer's declared intent states the z-load is a person leaning on the free arm; magnitude is not specified numerically anywhere in the spec or design intent, so it is not determined by the specification (UNBOUND). A representative magnitude range of 300-1500 N covers typical hand/body-leaning loads used in bracket service-load conventions, with 750 N as a defensible mid-range probe.
add_out_of_plane_hand_load_case.description: Adds a second declared load case representing the out-of-plane (z-direction) hand load applied during assembly/maintenance, alongside the existing in-plane y-load. This requires the geometry model to be extruded_3d (z loads are only representable in that model), so this operation also switches geometry.model accordingly. The stress constraint machinery (add_stress_constraints) is expected to evaluate its clustered stress constraint over the union of spec.load_cases, so appending this case makes the constraint multi-case-consistent rather than single-case.

switch_to_extruded_3d_model.parameter_source: Engineer notes state thickness is a free design choice; n_layers is a discretisation refinement of that free dimension not fixed by the spec, chosen here to give the 3D solid enough resolution to capture bending response to the out-of-plane z load.
switch_to_extruded_3d_model.description: Switches the geometry/analysis model from plane_stress (2 DOF/node, u,v only) to extruded_3d, and sets the number of through-thickness layers, so that out-of-plane loads (z-direction) produce a computable bending/through-thickness stress response instead of being kinematically unrepresentable.

set_initial_thickness.parameter_source: Stock range 1-20 mm stated explicitly by the engineer in the design intent notes ('stock is available from 1 mm to 20 mm and selecting a gauge is the designer's call'); probe_value of 6.0 mm chosen as a mid-range trial gauge to test leverage on stiffness/stress against the out-of-plane hand load.
set_initial_thickness.description: Sets the starting/current plate thickness away from the thinnest stock gauge (1 mm), placing it at a value within the full 1-20 mm stock range so that thickness is actively explored rather than left at its low-end default. This changes the value the geometry field holds; whether the optimizer subsequently treats it as free is governed by the mutable-geometry declaration, but moving it off the boundary default is the concrete, attributable change this operation makes.

set_thickness_to_stock_bound.parameter_source: Engineer's notes state stock plate is available from 1 mm to 20 mm and thickness is the designer's free choice; probing the upper bound of this stated range is the natural way to test whether the firm mass-fraction and stress-allowable constraints can jointly be satisfied for both load cases with the only free variable pushed as far as physically stocked, before concluding the constraint set is jointly infeasible.
set_thickness_to_stock_bound.description: Sets the free thickness variable to a specified value within the stated 1-20 mm stock range, so that the joint feasibility of the firm mass-fraction (0.3) and stress-allowable (350 MPa) constraints under both load cases (y primary + z hand load) can be probed at the boundary of the only remaining free variable, without altering the fixed envelope (L, arm_fraction) or either firm constraint. This isolates whether infeasibility, if any, is inherent to the coupled constraint set rather than a solvable modeling gap.
